content.title: About
content.content: Non-alcoholic wine is a beverage made from grapes with the alcohol removed or reduced to a very low level (usually below 0.5%). It retains the aromatic and flavor characteristics of traditional wine but without the intoxicating effect. Production methods include vacuum distillation, reverse osmosis, or fermentation followed by alcohol extraction.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first non-alcoholic wine, called "Mochiboo," appeared in Japan in the 1970s.
In the United States, non-alcoholic wine is often used in cooking as a substitute for regular wine in sauces and marinades.
Flavor profiles range from dry to sweet, similar to conventional wines.
Some brands add natural berry extracts and spices to enhance aroma.
Non-alcoholic wine is popular among pregnant women and those who abstain from alcohol for religious or health reasons.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Like regular wine, non-alcoholic wine contains polyphenols such as resveratrol, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Polysaccharides and flavonoids may improve vascular function without the risks associated with alcohol.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Non-alcoholic wine typically has fewer calories than its alcoholic counterpart, making it more diet‑friendly.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fermentation produces small amounts of B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, beneficial for metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Unlike alcoholic drinks, non-alcoholic wine does not cause dehydration and can contribute to fluid balance.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some sweet varieties may raise blood sugar levels.

items.title: Sulfite content
items.content: Like regular wine, it often contains sulfites, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Flavor enhancers and preservatives may be used; check the label if you have dietary restrictions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled as an aperitif, use in cocktails, or substitute for regular wine in cooking—sauces, risotto, and marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dark place with the cap tightly closed. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.
